tools.name: health
tools.description: Check whether the InfluxDB instance is ready for queries and writes, and read its version

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Get the InfluxDB user the API token belongs to (id, name, active status)

tools.name: list_orgs
tools.description: List the InfluxDB organizations the API token can see, optionally filtered to one organization name

org_name.description: Optional exact organization name to filter by

offset.description: Optional number of organizations to skip, for paging

tools.name: list_buckets
tools.description: List the buckets in the credential's InfluxDB organization, with their retention rules, optionally filtered to one bucket name

name.description: Optional exact bucket name to filter by

offset.description: Optional number of buckets to skip, for paging

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List the scheduled Flux tasks in the credential's InfluxDB organization, with their schedule, status and last run result

name.description: Optional exact task name to filter by

status.description: Optional task status to filter by

needs_review: NOT PROVEN BY ANY RUN. InfluxDB is a CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED HOST: base_url comes fromCredential 'url', so there is no public endpoint a shape-proof could reach and no proof artifact was written. Every path, query parameter and picked field name below is DOCUMENTARY, taken from the InfluxDB v2 API reference (https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2/api/v2/), not from a 2xx seen here. A wrong pick source yields empty output silently, so the LIVE harness against a real ephemeral influxdb:2 container is what must confirm them.

AUTH IS UNCHANGED FROM THE SCAFFOLD AND MATCHES THE VAULT: services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'influxdb' declares fields url, token and org, all three required, and its own testHeaders build `Authorization: Token ${creds.token}`. The spec's auth block is {type: header, header: Authorization, template: 'Token {{token}}'}, which is the same header the v2 API documents. The placeholder is {{token}} because that is the vault FIELD NAME; it is not an api_token field and was not renamed.
TEST PATH IS UNCHANGED: GET /api/v2/orgs is both the registry testEndpoint and a documented authenticated read, so there was nothing to correct.

THE FLUX QUERY ENDPOINT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED. POST /api/v2/query looks read-only but Flux is not: the language's own to() function WRITES points into a bucket (https://docs.influxdata.com/flux/v0/stdlib/influxdata/influxdb/to/), and the experimental http package can POST to arbitrary hosts, which is an egress hole as well as a write. Exposing an arbitrary-Flux tool to an agent would therefore ship a write and an SSRF behind a read-only-looking name. A second, independent blocker: the endpoint answers annotated CSV (text/csv), not JSON, so response.pick cannot address it at all. If Flux reads are ever wanted, the honest shape is a NARROW tool per question (buckets(), schema.measurements) with the Flux script built server-side from typed inputs, never a passthrough query string.

/health IS UNAUTHENTICATED on InfluxDB OSS v2. A 200 from the health tool proves the host, TLS and base_url, and NOTHING about the token. get_current_user (GET /api/v2/me) is the cheapest tool that does prove the token, and list_orgs is the one the vault already tests.

ORG SCOPING: list_buckets and list_tasks send the credential's org NAME as the `org` query parameter ({{org}}), which is required to scope reads on InfluxDB Cloud and filters correctly on OSS. list_orgs does NOT send it, because filtering the org list by the credential's own org would always return exactly one row and defeat the tool; its optional org_name input is a caller-supplied name filter instead.

CLAMPS come from the documented pagination ranges: buckets and orgs are limit default 20 / max 100, tasks is max 500 (the reference documents default 100; 20 is used here as the cheaper agent-facing default). The clamp helper always renders its default, so a limit is sent on every call even when the caller omits it.

LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: every tool carries a tool-level _probe. health and get_current_user take no inputs, so their _probe is deliberately EMPTY ({}) rather than absent, recording that nothing needs substituting. list_orgs probes org_name 'quoxproof-live' and list_buckets probes name 'quoxproof-live', the exact org and bucket name the live provisioner creates, so both resolve on a FRESH instance. list_tasks probes limit 5 only: a fresh instance has no tasks, so the honest expected result is a 200 with an empty tasks array, which proves routing and the container key but not the row shape. No credential is ever hinted.

get_bucket BY ID IS NOT MODELLED, ON PURPOSE: GET /api/v2/buckets/{bucketID} needs a bucket ID, and no ID is knowable on a fresh instance, so it could carry no probe that resolves. Fetching a bucket by name is already covered by list_buckets with the name filter.

AUTHORIZATIONS ARE NOT MODELLED, ON PURPOSE: GET /api/v2/authorizations lists API tokens and, for the token that created them, has historically returned the token VALUE in the response body. A read tool that can echo credentials back through an agent transcript is not a read tool worth shipping.

READ-ONLY by design: all five tools are GET and carry write:false. The v2 API's create, update and delete routes for buckets, orgs, tasks, dashboards, checks and the whole /api/v2/write path are not modelled.

rateLimit 30/min is a LOCAL courtesy and spend guard, not an InfluxData number. InfluxDB OSS applies no request rate limit of its own; InfluxDB Cloud enforces per-plan read and write limits that are far tighter than this, so a Cloud credential can hit a provider 429 before this limiter trips.
